These results indicate that the principal contribution lies in leakage-controlled multi-view probability representation and rigorous optimization/robustness ablation rather than an HPWOA-specific predictive advantage. External and transformer-disjoint validation remain necessary before cross-utility generalization can be claimed.

nodes.name: Land Use Land Cover (LULC) Change Detection in Delhi NCT Using Multi-Sensor Satellite Data and Google Earth Engine
nodes.venue: International Journal of Science and Research (IJSR)

nodes.name: International Journal of Science and Research (IJSR)
Interpretable detection-based image classification for differential diagnosis of vaginal discharge using smartphone-assisted microscopy
nodes.venue: Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence
nodes.abstract: Background The vaginal discharge is a common clinical presentation associated with diverse infectious and microbiota-related conditions. Existing artificial intelligence (AI)-based diagnostic approaches have predominantly focused on detection of individual pathogens and have rarely integrated microbiota-associated conditions within a diagnostic framework. We developed an explainable deep learning framework for automated analysis of Gram-stained vaginal smear images acquired using handheld smartphones or tablets positioned over a conventional light microscope eyepiece. Methods The framework integrates object detection with image-level classification, termed detection-based image classification, to identify diagnostically relevant microscopic structures without requiring exhaustive enumeration of all objects. Five diagnostic categories included vulvovaginal candidiasis (VVC), bacterial vaginosis (BV), trichomoniasis (TV), gonococcal urethritis/cervicitis (GU), and healthy vaginal condition (HL). YOLOv26, RT-DETR and EfficientDet0 were independently trained and evaluated using 1,966 microscopic images comprising 11,069 annotated diagnostic objects. Model explainability and computational benchmarking were assessed. The localization quality was independently evaluated by eight clinicians and microbiologists. Results Class-specific analysis demonstrated that TV and GU consistently achieved the highest detection performance across all models (mAP50 = 0.622–0.752), whereas RT-DETR demonstrated superior performance for VVC, BV, and HL. Expert evaluation showed favorable localization, with Good/Excellent ratings in 84.8 and 85.1% of valid evaluations for YOLOv26 and RT-DETR, respectively, with no significant difference between models (OR = 0.97; 95% CI, 0.58–1.61; p = 0.895). Conclusion This study presents an accurate and clinically interpretable framework that integrates microbiota-associated conditions and sexually transmitted infections for differential diagnosis of vaginal discharge using conventional light microscopy. By linking image-level predictions to localized diagnostic morphology, the framework provides human-verifiable AI evidence as a proof-of-concept prototype. While promising for low-cost implementation, rigorous prospective multi-center validation is required before broad clinical deployment or autonomous diagnosis.

nodes.name: Integrating multispectral satellite data and geomorphology for secondary iron mineral mapping in the Sierra Minera de Cartagena-La Unión (SE Spain)
nodes.venue: Revista de Teledetección
nodes.abstract: The Sierra Minera de Cartagena-La Unión (SE Spain) is a historical mining district where acid mine drainage (AMD) continues to impact soils and water resources. This study, on the one hand, maps three of the secondary iron minerals linked to AMD processes—hematite, goethite, and jarosite—using Sentinel-2 multispectral imagery and, on the other, evaluates how their spatial distribution relates to geomorphological processes and landform configuration. Three spectral techniques were applied: band ratio, minimum wavelength mapper, and a parabola fitting technique. Seventy-four field samples were analysed using X-ray diffraction (XRD) to validate mineral identification. Results indicate that the parabola fitting technique provided the most reliable classification. Sentinel-2 successfully distinguished the three minerals despite its multispectral resolution, due to its red-edge bands capturing diagnostic VNIR features associated with iron-bearing mineral spectral features. Integration of mineral maps with landform units mapped through aerial photointerpretation revealed a strong geomorphological control on AMD mineral deposition: hematite dominates well-drained depositional environments such as alluvial fans, while jarosite and goethite concentrate in colluvial slopes, drainage channels, marshes, and substratum units affected by sulphide oxidation and intermittent moisture conditions

nodes.name: Informal Urban Expansion Under Displacement: A Spatial–Relational Analysis of Building Patterns
nodes.abstract: Abstract Understanding how informal urban expansion unfolds under displacement pressure is essential for planning and governance in conflict-affected cities where conventional data and planning instruments are unavailable. Existing quantitative approaches to urban morphology tend to analyse buildings as isolated entities or rely on predefined spatial contexts, limiting their capacity to capture the relational processes through which informal settlements emerge and adapt. This study introduces an analytical framework that integrates Morphological Cells with an unsupervised Graph Attention Network (GAT) to jointly model building-level morphometrics and inter-building spatial relationships. Applied to nearly 50,000 manually digitised buildings in Marib, Yemen, the framework identifies 13 morphological clusters that consolidate into four process-driven urban patterns: displacement-driven densification, tenure-enabled incremental expansion, semi-formal historic continuity, and transitional hybridisation. A controlled comparison against morphology-only and ablation baselines at identical cluster counts (K = 13) confirms that incorporating relational topology produces a fundamentally different classification (Adjusted Rand Index = 0.067 relative to the morphology-only baseline), with substantially greater spatial coherence aligned to documented displacement dynamics. Stability analysis across ten independent training runs indicates that while individual building assignments are sensitive to initialisation, the macro-level taxonomy of four super-types remains structurally recoverable. The findings demonstrate that informal expansion under displacement follows structured spatial logics shaped by tribal land tenure, humanitarian material restrictions, and caste-based exclusion, rather than chaotic sprawl. By transforming building footprints into a cadastral-free diagnostic tool for adaptive urban processes, the framework offers transferable insights for context-sensitive governance in cities where formal planning capacity has collapsed.

nodes.name: In-flight magnitude of “the leans” illusion in pilots deprived of visual cues: An exploratory study
nodes.venue: Perception
nodes.abstract: “ The leans” is a spatial illusion encountered by pilots flying without reliable visual references. It can occur when a pilot promptly returns to straight-and-level flight after unawarely having entered a banked turn. The return to straight-and-level flight is sensed by the semicircular canals and erroneously perceived as banking in the opposite direction. The purpose was to establish (1) the magnitude and interindividual variability of the leans, and (2) if centrifuge-based spatial-orientation (SO) training, improving roll-tilt assessment, would affect the illusion. In a fighter-jet-trainer aircraft, pilots ( n = 10) were sitting in darkness and setting a luminous line parallel with their imagined horizon, while being exposed to a gradual entering of a 15–20° banked turn, followed by a prompt return to straight-and-level flight. Measurements were performed before and after a 4-week period, during which five of the pilots undertook a 9 × 1 h SO-training regimen. During the pre-training trial, the pilots perceived on average 47% (range = 0–140%) of the roll-angular displacement encountered during the transition from the turn to level flight, i.e., they perceived being roll-tilted 10 ± 9° in the opposite direction. SO-training did not affect the leans magnitude ( p = .84). The results confirm anecdotal accounts of marked interindividual variability of the leans illusion, and suggest that such variability in the canal-induced illusion exists even without perceptual interference from visual input.

nodes.name: Hyperspectral Retrieval of Winter Wheat Leaf Area Index and Canopy Chlorophyll Content: Evaluating Simulation Design and Measured-Data Adaptation
nodes.venue: Remote Sensing
nodes.abstract: How retrieval performance varies with simulation settings, neural architecture, and measured-data adaptation remains unclear for hyperspectral crop trait retrieval. Here, we evaluated winter wheat leaf area index (LAI) and canopy chlorophyll content (CCC) retrieval using two simulated datasets and four dual-branch neural architectures. Models were pretrained on two PROSAIL-D datasets with default and previously optimized leaf-angle settings and then adapted separately to ground and unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) observations. Evaluation used five repetitions with physical-plot grouping, with approximately 30% of plot groups allocated to measured-data adaptation. Simulation-trained random forest (RF) and partial least squares regression served as baselines without measured-data adaptation. Adaptation reduced mean test root mean square error (RMSE) in all 32 neural model–dataset–target–platform combinations relative to direct simulation-based prediction. Dataset II, which used the previously optimized leaf-angle setting, reduced mean RMSE in 13 of 16 neural configurations before adaptation and 11 of 16 afterwards. No neural architecture was uniformly best. RF achieved the highest mean R2 in seven of eight simulation-only tasks and outperformed the adapted Dataset II CNN–Transformer on both UAV targets. Despite adaptation gains, all adapted neural configurations retained negative mean R2 for UAV CCC. These findings support measured-data adaptation within the tested protocol, while showing that the effects of simulation design and architecture are task dependent and that relative improvements do not necessarily imply adequate absolute predictive accuracy.

nodes.name: FusionLite-DETR: A Lightweight Transformer-Based Model for UAV-Based Insulator Defect Detection
nodes.venue: Sensors
nodes.abstract: Aiming to overcome the challenges associated with the unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-based inspection of transmission line insulators, including the tiny scale of defect regions, irregular morphologies, and low contrast with complex backgrounds, we propose a lightweight insulator defect detection model based on real-time detection transformer (RT-DETR), termed FusionLite-DETR. To improve detection accuracy while maintaining computational efficiency, the proposed model introduces systematic enhancements to RT-DETR in four aspects: the backbone network, feature reconstruction operator, feature fusion module, and loss function. Firstly, the backbone network is reconstructed by integrating deformable large kernel attention (DLKA) into VanillaNet, enabling the model to couple global perception with precise local focusing, thereby significantly enhancing feature extraction for multi-scale defects. Secondly, the defect-aware content-aware reassembly of features (DA-CARAFE), is proposed to replace the conventional upsampling method. It dynamically generates reassembly convolution kernels based on underlying spatial features, achieving semantically aligned feature fusion under lightweight constraints. Meanwhile, a wavelet transform-based C3 (WTC3), is designed. By performing feature representation and interaction across different frequency sub-bands and incorporating ghost-shuffle convolution (GSConv), the module effectively reduces parameter redundancy while preserving critical high-frequency texture information. Furthermore, by introducing the inner minimum point distance intersection over union (Inner-MPDIoU) loss function, the boundary discrepancies are accurately captured by combining auxiliary-box overlap measurement with vertex-based geometric distance constraints, thus effectively mitigating the gradient vanishing problem for distant small targets during regression. FusionLite-DETR achieved mean average precision at an intersection-over-union threshold of 0.50 (mAP50) values of 95.5% and 93.1% on the private multi-scenario insulator defect dataset (PMID) and insulator fault detection dataset IFDD (datasets), respectively, with 19.1 M parameters and a computational cost of 54.8 giga floating-point operations (GFLOPs). Compared with RT-DETR with a resnet-50 backbone (RT-DETR-R50), the proposed model reduced the parameter count and GFLOPs by 54.8% and 57.4%, respectively, demonstrating a favorable balance between detection performance and model complexity.

nodes.name: From cloud optical thickness to solar radiation: deep spatiotemporal forecasting with geostationary satellite imagery
nodes.abstract: Abstract. Accurate short-term cloud forecasting is essential for solar radiation and solar energy applications, where rapidly evolving cloud fields introduce substantial variability in surface solar irradiance. In this study, we develop a hybrid ConvLSTM-UNet deep learning model for 15-min-ahead forecasting of cloud optical thickness (COT) from Meteosat/SEVIRI observations over Europe. The model combines multiscale spatial feature extraction with recurrent spatiotemporal learning and employs a combined Charbonnier–SSIM loss to improve both numerical accuracy and the preservation of cloud structures. The proposed forecasting model is evaluated against real COT satellite retrievals and benchmarked against persistence and a dense optical flow cloud motion vector (CMV) approach. For 15-min-ahead forecasts, ConvLSTM-UNet achieves lower COT prediction errors and higher perceptual quality than both benchmarks, with MAE and RMSE of 1.25 and 9.52, respectively, and SSIM of 0.95. The impact of COT forecast errors on solar radiation is further assessed through the cloud modification factor (CMF), for which the proposed model achieves a forecast skill of approximately 30 % relative to persistence. Its performance advantage is particularly evident under cloudy and rapidly evolving conditions, and remains evident under recursive forecasts extending to approximately 165 min ahead. These results demonstrate the potential of deep spatiotemporal learning for satellite-based short-term cloud and solar radiation forecasting.

nodes.name: Foveated metamers of the early visual system
nodes.venue: eLife
nodes.abstract: The ability of humans to discriminate and identify spatial patterns varies across the visual field and is generally worse in the periphery than in the fovea. This decline in performance is revealed in many kinds of tasks, from detection to recognition. A parsimonious hypothesis is that the representation of any visual feature is blurred (spatially averaged) by an amount that differs for each feature, but that in all cases increases with eccentricity. Here, we examine models for two such features: local luminance and spectral energy. Each model averages the corresponding feature in pooling windows whose diameters scale linearly with eccentricity. We performed perceptual experiments with synthetic stimuli to determine the largest window scaling for which human and model discrimination abilities match (the ‘critical’ scaling). We used much larger stimuli than those of previous studies, subtending 53.6 by 42.2° of visual angle. We found that the critical scaling for the luminance model was approximately one-fourth that of the energy model and, consistent with earlier studies, that the estimated critical scaling value was smaller when discriminating a synthesized stimulus from a natural image than when discriminating two synthesized stimuli. Moreover, we found that initializing the generation of the synthesized images with natural images reduced the critical scaling value when discriminating two synthesized stimuli, but not when discriminating a synthesized from a natural image stimulus. Together, the results show that critical scaling is strongly affected by the image statistic (pooled luminance vs. spectral energy), the comparison type (synthesized vs. synthesized or synthesized vs. natural), and the initialization image for synthesis (white noise vs. natural image). We offer a coherent explanation for these results in terms of alignments and misalignments of the models with human perceptual representations.

nodes.name: Fatigue Driving Detection Based On Multimodal EEG Feature Fusion
nodes.abstract: Abstract Preventing and reducing traffic accidents is an urgent necessity for safeguarding public safety and societal development. Fatigued driving, as one of the core contributing factors, necessitates effective monitoring. Therefore, addressing issues such as weak model generalisation capability, complex parameter tuning, and difficulties in extracting EEG signal features within existing fatigued driving detection technologies, this paper proposes a multi-modal EEG feature fusion-based driving fatigue detection model (MEFD-Net). This model comprises three sub-networks: (1) A time-domain feature extraction network utilises an enhanced BiLSTM with GeLU activation to capture temporal dynamics; (2) A time-invariant feature extraction network employs weighted adaptive multi-scale convolutions combined with residual connections and self-attention mechanisms; (3) The spatial-frequency domain feature extraction network employs a pure convolutional architecture to extract spatial-frequency domain features. By integrating multi-dimensional EEG features, MEFD-Net achieves end-to-end classification without manual feature selection, enhancing both classification accuracy and fault tolerance. Experiments demonstrate that the proposed model exhibits superior performance in processing complex, unstable EEG signals, achieving average improvements of 7.09%, 5.56%, and 4.38% in detection accuracy, recall, and F1 score respectively, outperforming existing mainstream algorithms.

nodes.name: Evaluation of L-Band SMAP Scatterometer Tropical Cyclone Wind Retrieval Using UHR σ° Measurements
nodes.venue: Remote Sensing
nodes.abstract: Tropical cyclones pose a significant hazard to coastal populations and shipping infrastructure. By helping provide timely warnings, ocean scatterometers can mitigate this threat with ocean wind estimates. In this study, the Soil Moisture Active/Passive (SMAP) mission is used to evaluate the effectiveness of wind estimates using L-band scatterometry for tropical cyclones. Standard-resolution SMAP scatterometer normalized radar backscatter (σ∘) measurements are enhanced to a much finer spatial resolution using the Ultra-High Resolution (UHR) algorithm, from which high-to-severe winds are estimated. The influence of σ∘ polarization (Horizontal HH-, Vertical VV-, and Cross X-pol) on wind estimates at high-to-severe winds is assessed. In this study, a new wind model is created with tropical cyclone Best-Track data, SMAP σ∘ measurements, and Numerical Weather Prediction winds. The Best-Track-derived wind model and SMAP UHR σ∘ measurements are used to create a Geophysical Model Function (GMF), and wind retrieval is performed. Analysis of wind retrieval estimates demonstrates that the HH- and VV-pol σ∘ tend to saturate at high-to-severe winds while X-pol measurements do not. Retrieved UHR winds generally align with the Best-Track derived wind model, although the errors can exceed desirable tolerances for speed and direction (i.e., less than 10% m/s and 20° Root Mean Square Error). Ultimately, these results suggest that L-band scatterometer wind estimation has potential for tropical cyclone monitoring by increasing the SNR of X-pol σ∘ measurements.

nodes.name: Cross-Condition Prediction of Pointwise Surface Settlement Using Key Tunneling Parameter Selection and Transfer Learning
nodes.venue: Symmetry
nodes.abstract: Construction-stage surface settlement prediction becomes challenging under changing geological conditions and limited monitoring data in target sections. This study proposes a cross-condition prediction framework integrating key tunneling parameter selection and transfer learning using shield construction data from Chengdu Metro Line 18. The prediction target is the pointwise cumulative surface settlement associated with a specific monitoring point and shield ring state. Ring-level operational records and settlement observations are temporally aligned, while grouped spatial-block splitting is adopted to preserve spatial dependence among samples. Key tunneling parameters are identified by combining Random Forest importance, SHAP or permutation importance, Slime Mould Algorithm optimization, Spearman correlation, and engineering interpretation. A Transfer Multilayer Perceptron is then constructed through source-domain pretraining, parameter transfer, and target-domain fine-tuning. Results show that the proposed T-MLP achieves an MAE of 3.18 mm, an RMSE of 4.08 mm, and an R2 of 0.852 in the target domain, reducing MAE by 39.54% relative to direct source-domain prediction. The framework provides an effective data-driven approach for cross-condition settlement prediction under limited target-domain observations.

nodes.name: Assessment and Monitoring of Post-Fire Recovery Using Satellite Imagery and the Stability Index in the North West of Algeria
nodes.abstract: Abstract Forest fire is phenomeno difficult to model because depend on many parameters, which vary in both time and space. It is therefore necessary to carry research and prevention actions as part of the improvement and management of this risk. The severity of wildfires due to hotter and drier global climate conditions affects ecological resilience and ecosystems at risk of deterioration following the failure of post-fire recovery. To properly prepare for wildfires, it is crucial to determine fire-sensitive areas, then locate fire suppression structures, and assess the spatial and temporal quantification of post-fire regeneration. The objectives of this study is fire detection using remote sensing and GIS, and make model to monitor the recovery of vegetation by using satellite imagery and the post-fire stability index. While undisturbed or recovered system states are characterized by rates of change close to zero. This reflects the typical pattern of decreasing change rates in post-fire recovery trajectories. For this, time series analyses of remote sensing images from Landsat between 2013 and 2020, both pre- and post-fire, were conducted in the Sidi Bel Abbés region, Algeria, and for the post-fire stability index, we used NBR and NBR2 as the base spectral indices to evaluate the post-fire stability index. therefore demonstrate the performance and relevance of the post-fire stability index compared to alternative approaches because this stability index provides a relatively simple and practical solution for consistent large-scale monitoring of post-fire recovery with satellite image. thus offers numerous opportunities for further research on fires, and forest recovery.

nodes.name: Artificial intelligence for medication recognition and safety: a systematic review of detection, classification, OCR, and digital health applications
nodes.venue: Frontiers in Digital Health
nodes.abstract: Introduction Medication errors and adverse drug events remain causes of patient harm, underscoring the need for technologies supporting medication identification, verification, and medication safety. Artificial intelligence (AI), computer vision, optical character recognition (OCR), and digital health technologies are applied to medication recognition. Objective To systematically review AI-based medication recognition systems and characterize recognition tasks, computational approaches, datasets, evaluation, validation, generalizability, deployment, applications, and emerging directions. Methods A systematic review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020. Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, and PubMed/MEDLINE were searched for publications from 1 January 2016 to 4 September 2026, using two conceptual blocks covering medication recognition and AI methods. Of 895 retrieved records, 136 duplicates were removed, and 759 records underwent screening. After full-text assessment, 14 reports were excluded, and 91 studies were included. Title-and-abstract screening yielded 84.72% observed agreement (Cohen’s κ = 0.527 ). For methodological assessment, both reviewers independently applied D1–D8 to the 91 included studies before consensus resolution. Across 728 domain-level assessments, observed agreement was 97.66%, with an aggregate Cohen’s κ of 0.959; domain-specific κ values ranged from 0.857 to 1.000. Evidence was synthesized through cross-study analysis and four evidence maps. Results Evidence shows use of detection, classification, OCR/imprint recognition, hybrid and multimodal architectures, alongside few-shot, low-shot, zero-shot, and incremental learning. Applications extend to assistive, mobile, and IoT-enabled systems, medication verification, and clinical decision support. Heterogeneity in datasets, imaging conditions, evaluation protocols, and validation strategies limits comparison and generalizability. External validation, cross-dataset testing, unseen-medication evaluation, prospective deployment, and clinical testing remain limited. Conclusion AI-based medication recognition is evolving from a computer vision task into a digital informatics component supporting medication safety, accessibility, verification, and patient care. Future research should prioritize diverse datasets, leakage control, independent multicenter validation, unseen-medication evaluation, explainable and privacy-preserving AI, interoperability, and resource-efficient deployment. Evaluation should extend beyond accuracy to clinical utility, safety, usability, trust, and patient-centered outcomes.

nodes.name: Application of Sentinel-2 Multispectral Satellite Imagery in Lithological Mapping: A Case Study of Meda Kebele and Its Surroundings, Ethiopia
nodes.abstract: Lithological identification and mapping are crucial in understanding geological processes, mineral exploration, natural resource management, land-use planning, and other applications. Conventional field-focused mapping of geology is often requiring a lot of time and expensive, particularly in remote and rugged terrains, like in our area. Recent advances in satellite remote sensing provide efficient tools for lithological discrimination. This study explores the application of Sentinel-2 multispectral imagery to develop a lithological map in a case of Meda kebele. The Sentinel-2 satellite image was classified by using support vector machine (SVM) classification system to prepare a excellent geological map, which was validated by previous geological maps and field surveys For this purpose, several band combinations, spectral indices, and image processing methods, including OIF, ICA and PCA, were used in order to enhance the contrast among different rocks. Following that, a supervised classification supported by field survey and previous lithological maps of the area was carried out to create a lithological map. The results show that Sentinel-2 imagery can distinguish between the common geological units found in the area, which include metavolcanics, basalt, dolomite, limestone, marble, slate and sandstone, due to it has good spatial resolution of 10- 60 m and vast spectral extent from VNIR-SWIR. This paper highlights the significance of Sentinel-2 data for regional geological mapping, giving baseline information for mineral prospecting and resource management in Meda kebele.

nodes.name: Agentic AIGC: A Survey of Visual Generation Agents
nodes.abstract: Visual generation is becoming a general component of AI infrastructure, supporting content creation across design, entertainment, education, science, and industry. Generative and multimodal models have substantially improved single-pass synthesis. At the same time, multi-step visual creation requires spatial precision, identity persistence, temporal coherence, editable structure, factual fidelity, and physical plausibility throughout the creation process. Errors in intermediate artifacts can propagate across subsequent steps, making creation control a central requirement. Model scaling, prompt refinement, additional conditioning, and repeated sampling improve individual outputs; coordinating these capabilities across a task requires runtime evidence to influence subsequent creation decisions. Within AI-generated content (AIGC), we use Agentic AIGC to describe goal-driven content creation organized through a multi-step control loop. This survey focuses on visual generation agents: systems that use runtime evidence from evolving visual artifacts, task environments, and interaction histories to change later creation-relevant action selection or parameterization, including generation, editing, verification, recovery, replanning, and stopping. The defining behavioral property is therefore an observation--action dependency: runtime observations change later action selection. Whether those decisions improve task or constraint outcomes is evaluated separately with matched tools and resource budgets. We organize this emerging field around the control mechanisms and behavioral evidence that connect generative capabilities to autonomous visual creation. Specifically, we formalize this boundary and characterize autonomy through five cumulative levels (L1--L5). A six-component analytical framework (goal understanding, specification, and planning; memory; tool; perception; action; and cross-task self-improvement) structures a cross-domain comparison spanning image, video, 3D/CAD, scientific visualization, structured documents, UI/Web, and related visual-creation domains. Building on this comparison, we analyze training from trajectory supervision and policy initialization through reinforcement learning from multimodal and executable feedback to experience reuse with skill abstraction and transfer. We organize evaluation into four complementary levels: artifact quality, goal and constraint satisfaction, trajectory and decision quality, and system and human-centered evaluation. This synthesis distinguishes behavioral evidence from evidence that feedback improves a creation outcome. Finally, we identify research directions in the scope of visual agency, reliable long-horizon control, cross-task improvement, and evaluation.

nodes.name: Advancing Mangrove Forest Mapping Using Super-Resolution and Semantic Segmentation of Multi-Date Multi-Sensor Satellite Imagery: Applications in East and West Africa
nodes.venue: Remote Sensing
nodes.abstract: Remote sensing is essential for mapping mangrove forest ecosystems, yet accuracy and spatial resolution remain limited, particularly in Africa, where mangroves are fragmented, reference data and cloud-free images are scarce. The state-of-the-art of mangrove forest mapping relies on native-resolution imagery using machine learning. This study evaluates deep learning methods using aggregated multi-date satellite imagery to improve mangrove mapping and national-scale area estimation. Super-resolution and semantic segmentation techniques were applied to Sentinel-2 (S2) and Sentinel-1 (S1) images, with training data derived from field observations and high-resolution drone and satellite imagery. Coastal regions of Tanzania and Ghana were used as representative study areas for eastern and western Africa, respectively. Results show strong classification performance, with S2 imagery alone achieving an Intersection over Union (IoU) of 85.8%. Adding S1 provided modest gains (IoU 86.3%), while super-resolution significantly improved the accuracy (IoU 88.5%). The combined super-resolved S2 and S1 dataset yielded the highest performance (IoU 89.2%). Wall-to-wall mapping and statistically rigorous validation and area estimation produced accurate results with quantified uncertainty. Tanzania showed high consistency (F1 = 96%; 1207 km2, 95% CI [1151.7, 1263]), while Ghana exhibited slightly higher uncertainty (F1 = 92%; 92.6 km2, 95% CI [87.5, 97.7]). Integrating deep learning with multi-date, multi-sensor fusion and super-resolution enables accurate mangrove mapping and area estimation for improved coastal management and restoration.

nodes.name: Adaptive Margin Based Metric Learning for Unbalanced Point Cloud Classification and Retrieval
nodes.abstract: Abstract Loss function plays a crucial role in modern deep learning based 3D object classification and retrieval methods The widely used softmax loss relies on an implicit hypothesis that all classes have sufficient samples and intraclass feature spaces are separated by a uniform margin yet real world large scale 3D object datasets are highly unbalanced making it challenging for softmax loss to simultaneously ensure intraclass compactness and interclass discrepancy To address this issue we propose an adaptive margin based loss function for point cloud learning from highly unbalanced datasets which to the best of our knowledge is the first work introducing margin based metric learning into point cloud classification and retrieval thus achieving good adaptation to unbalanced 3D datasets Additionally the loss function incorporates regularization constraints on weight vectors To enable cross layer feature interaction and enhance network capacity we also design a hierarchical bilinear pooling strategy across layers and a lightweight spatial transform module Extensive experiments on ModelNet40 and ShapeNetCore55 datasets demonstrate that our method with very low computational cost outperforms state of the art approaches based on multiple 3D object representations.

nodes.name: A Thermoelectric Hydrogel-Based Insole with Self-Decoupled Temperature and Pressure Sensing for Diabetic Plantar Monitoring
nodes.venue: Nano Letters
nodes.abstract: Abstract Plantar temperature and pressure reflect the plantar health status of diabetic patients and serve as critical indicators for evaluating disease progression. However, existing plantar monitoring devices are still limited by single-modal signal acquisition, bulky device configurations, and a strong reliance on external power supplies. Herein, we report a thermogalvanic hydrogel-based smart insole integrating self-powered sensing units for self-decoupled plantar monitoring. The insole integrates 16 self-decoupled thermogalvanic hydrogel sensing units, which convert plantar temperature difference and pressure stimuli into decouplable electrical signals via the thermogalvanic effect and the active iontronic piezoresistive effect, respectively. The incorporation of the backend acquisition circuit into the smart monitoring insole enables remote plantar temperature-difference and pressure mapping. Cloud-based machine learning further empowers the insole to assess plantar status in diabetic patients and distinguish disease-associated gait patterns. This work provides a versatile strategy for developing multimodal intelligent wearable platforms for personalized foot health monitoring and disease management.

nodes.name: A Reproducible Normalization Model for Forensic Analysis of Heterogeneous Bank Statements: Design and Internal-Consistency Evaluation on a Synthetic Corpus
nodes.venue: Journal of Cybersecurity and Privacy
nodes.abstract: Bank statements are information-rich but labour-intensive forensic sources: differing formats, inconsistent field naming, incomplete counterparty attributes and mixed debit–credit conventions make cross-account comparison unsafe, and an automated summary is easily read later as established fact. We propose a reproducible normalization model converting heterogeneous statement records into one auditable transaction journal, each row bound to its source line. It separates the source document, the normalized record and the interpretive indicator, formalizes an eight-stage cycle from inventory and hash control to quality control and indicator generation, and attaches an evidential status to every reconstructed route. The evaluation is entirely synthetic: the corpus, whose defects have known type and position, was generated by the same authors who built the control layer, so the scores below are an internal-consistency check rather than evidence of performance on real bank exports. The corpus, its generator and a reference implementation of the model are released with the article. Across 1200 transactions from 30 files and 15 layouts, all 8 mandatory fields map completely while counterparty identifiers reach 0.573. The control layer flags 55 of the 57 injected defects with no false candidate; the two misses are undetectable by construction and are reported as such. Reclassifying one channel-only record changes precision from 1.000 to 0.982 and F1 from 0.982 to 0.973. On eight fault types the generator never produces, seven are surfaced in the defect log and one, a day–month swap, passes largely unnoticed. On data with no planted behavior, the indicators flag from none to 11 of 12 subjects depending on the threshold, so thresholds need calibration against a reference population. Removing the lineage tuple or the defect log leaves detection unchanged while removing source references or suppressing some logged warnings, showing that detection scores alone do not describe the output’s auditability. Validation on real exports and review by independent assessors remain open.

nodes.name: A Multimodal Attention-Based Deep Learning Framework for Sweetpotato Production Prediction in Batanes, Philippines
nodes.abstract: Abstract Accurate agricultural production prediction could enable planning, allocation of resources, and adaptation to different environmental conditions. This study evaluates SweetPotatoProdNet , a multimodal attention-based deep learning framework for predicting sweetpotato (Ipomoea batatas) , locally known as wakay , production in Batanes Province, Philippines. SweetPotatoProdNet considers meteorological, soil, satellite-based vegetation, and agricultural-related information in the form of modality-specific feature embedding, attention-based fusion, and multilayer regression head. The final modeling dataset comprised 1,463 observations spanning January 2022 to December 2025. Weather observations provided the primary modeling index, while Sentinel-2 imagery was processed at five-day intervals and soil nutrient and related agricultural data were available weekly; these heterogeneous sources were temporally aligned to the modeling observation dates. The target variable is the total production volume in terms of metric tons (MT). On the reported test partition, the proposed architecture achieved MAE = 4.7000 MT, MSE = 35.8800 MT², RMSE = 5.9900 MT, and R² = 0.7800, outperforming the reported LightGBM, voting ensemble, random forest, XGBoost, and support vector regression baselines on all four metrics. The study is intentionally constrained to the available Batanes dataset, reported predictor modalities, and reported comparative results, and does not make claims of external validation, prospective deployment, and does not report LSTM, GRU, SHAP, ablation, walk-forward, and extreme-condition analyses. The findings suggest the potential of multimodal attention-based learning for localized agricultural production prediction, and the necessity of independent validation prior to wider deployment.

nodes.name: A Cloud-Native Google Earth Engine Framework for Water Accounting Land Use (WALU) Classification: Application to the Narmada River Basin
nodes.venue: Water
nodes.abstract: Sustainable management of river basins requires land and water to be understood as a single interacting system, yet the land-use datasets most widely used in basin planning primarily represent physical land cover and rarely distinguish hydrologically distinct land uses, grouping hydrologically distinct pixels (e.g., rainfed and irrigated cropland, or natural and engineered water bodies) into a single undifferentiated class. The Water Accounting Land Use (WALU) classification of the Water Accounting Plus (WA+) framework was designed to close this gap, but its conventional implementation has typically been implemented as a desktop workflow that loads complete rasters into local memory, which limits its efficiency for large basins and fine-resolution inputs. This study addresses that constraint by re-engineering the WA+ WALU workflow as a cloud-native, server-side classification on Google Earth Engine, integrating nine geospatial input layers through a hierarchical rule-based fusion that implements the original WA+ classification rules, each checked against the desktop implementation, while avoiding the need to load complete raster datasets into local memory and providing a scripted workflow that can be re-run by other users. The 24-class, pixel-level WALU map of the 97,366 km2 Narmada River Basin reveals that the human-modified land uses Modified Land Use (MLU) and Managed Water Use (MWU) (51.5%) marginally exceed the natural and semi-natural land uses Protected Land Use (PLU) and Utilized Land Use (ULU) (48.5%). Irrigated cereals (MWU3; 32.21%) form the largest WALU class, exceeding closed deciduous forest (23.41%), which indicates a strong dependence of agricultural production on irrigation and increased engineered water regime. The classification also maps wasteland over 9.91% of the basin, providing a spatially explicit basis for prioritizing land-restoration assessments, and shows marked sub-basin and district-scale differences in land use, with irrigated cropland concentrated in about ten districts within the major reservoir command areas against a periphery of rainfed and degraded land. A two-level accuracy assessment, combining a stratified confusion-matrix analysis (86.4% area-weighted accuracy; Kappa = 0.82) with a Sentinel-2 NDVI (Normalized Difference Vegetation Index) phenological validation of the rainfed-irrigated split (Cohen’s d = 1.27), indicates that the map is suitable as a land-use input for basin-scale WA+ accounting at the aggregated class level. The framework can be adapted for WALU mapping across other data-scarce basins.

nodes.name: Robotic grasping of hollow guardrail components for outdoor installation: a geometry-based RGB-D depth sampling approach for 3D localization
nodes.venue: Industrial Robot: the international journal of robotics research and application
nodes.abstract: Purpose This study aims to develop an integrated sensing–perception–control system for automated highway guardrail installation, addressing the depth perception failure of RGB-D cameras over hollow structural regions in field working conditions. Design/methodology/approach An edge-exterior multilayer depth sampling strategy with 72 points on three concentric rings is proposed to obtain reliable surface depth from the solid body surrounding the hollow aperture under oblique viewing and partial occlusion. A lightweight segmentation model, YOLOv11n-PMS-seg, adopts a feature optimization–attention enhancement–shape constraint design, supported by ellipse fitting, Kalman filtering, track-ID recovery and adaptive CAN transmission. A one-time teaching step records the relative pose between the gripper and hole; the manipulator servos to this reference, eliminating explicit hand-eye calibration and making grasping invariant to forklift position and guardrail height. Findings The depth acquisition success rate reaches 99.4%. Under a single calibration at 1,250 mm, localization error is 17.8 ± 4.2 mm at 30 fps. Across 200 outdoor winter trials (−5 to 5 °C), 194 were successful; the six failures manifested as system-level freezes rather than as erroneous perception output. For low-illumination indoor scenes, a 6 W LED supplementary light maintains depth quality. YOLOv11n-PMS-seg cuts parameters by 7.8% and GFLOPs by 10.7% while improving mAP@0.5:0.95 by 3.3 percentage points. Research limitations/implications The system is currently validated at a fixed vertical distance of 1,250 mm for single-target scenarios. Failure attribution relied on field observation, as automated telemetry logging was not implemented. Future work should address variable operating distances, multi-target grasping and onboard failure diagnosis to broaden deployment applicability. Practical implications The proposed system enables automated robotic grasping of hollow guardrail components with a 97.0% success rate under real outdoor conditions, directly reducing manual labor and safety risks in highway construction. Its lightweight architecture (17% GPU utilization) allows integration into existing industrial vehicle platforms without significant hardware upgrades, offering a cost-effective solution for infrastructure automation. Social implications Automating highway guardrail installation reduces worker exposure to traffic hazards and physically demanding labor in road construction environments. Validated outdoor winter deployment demonstrates the feasibility of year-round infrastructure maintenance, contributing to safer roads and more efficient use of construction resources in civil engineering applications. Originality/value This work presents an integrated grasping pipeline for hollow guardrail components that combines a geometry-based depth sampling strategy with a teaching-based relative-pose scheme, without relying on additional learning-based depth completion networks. Validation covers winter outdoor daytime conditions at a single calibration distance; rainfall, direct sunlight and other guardrail specifications remain future work.

nodes.name: Industrial Robot: the international journal of robotics research and application
DIGITAL ELECTORAL ADMINISTRATION AND ADMINISTRATIVE LEGITIMACY: AN INSTITUTIONAL TRANSLATION MODEL OF EVIDENCE-CALIBRATED RELIANCE
nodes.venue: FUGUS Journal of Public Administration and Management
nodes.abstract: Digital electoral administration increasingly structures voter registration, candidate and party administration, logistics, results information, and citizens’ interactions with electoral authorities. Technical functionality and information availability, however, are insufficient for judging whether electoral administration is competent, fair, credible, or legitimately exercised. This article develops an institutional translation model explaining how independently assessable administrative safeguards become usable evidence for public judgement. An integrative theory-building review synthesises 37 scholarly works, supplemented by six decisions of Indonesia’s General Elections Commission that serve only as an illustrative function–safeguard mapping rather than empirical validation of the model. Four safeguard families structure the framework: accuracy and reliability, status clarity and intelligibility, traceability and auditability, and correctability and remedy. Their public significance depends on evidence remaining accessible, attributable, intelligible, procedurally situated, and linked to identifiable institutional action. The article also introduces evidence-calibrated reliance to describe whether citizens adjust function-specific reliance in accordance with credible evidence of administrative performance. The synthesis distinguishes this concept from trust by treating correspondence between diagnostic evidence and reliance adjustment—not confidence itself—as the relevant outcome. Greater reliance is not invariably desirable; documented weaknesses may warrant verification, complaint, caution, or lawful contestation. Electoral-administration legitimacy ultimately depends on both institutional performance and the conditions that enable defensible public judgement.

nodes.name: FUGUS Journal of Public Administration and Management
Image-free ghost edge detection at ultra-low sampling rates via a Vision Mamba network
nodes.venue: Optics Letters
nodes.abstract: Edge detection is essential for extracting structural boundaries in visual scenes, but conventional deep-learning-based methods remain sensitive to degradations in the input images and involve redundant full-image acquisition. Image-free ghost edge detection provides an efficient alternative by directly extracting edge information from bucket measurements, yet existing methods still require relatively high sampling rates to obtain reliable edge maps. Here, using a Vision Mamba network within the ghost edge detection framework, we achieve image-free edge detection directly from bucket measurements at ultra-low sampling rates. By employing joint optimization of illumination patterns and network parameters, the proposed method achieves reliable edge extraction at a sampling rate as low as 0.39%, as demonstrated by both simulations and optical experiments. Furthermore, the demonstrated robustness to measurement noise and qualitative edge-recovery results for selected visually distinct targets indicate the potential of the proposed method under challenging measurement conditions. We envision this image-free ghost edge-detection framework as a prospective platform for efficient task-oriented imaging under severe measurement constraints.

nodes.name: Deep Learning and Foundation Models for Forest Remote Sensing
nodes.venue: Earth Observation for Forest Monitoring and Climate Action

nodes.name: Earth Observation for Forest Monitoring and Climate Action
Towards hydrological extreme event monitoring using deep learning-downscaled simulated NGGM and MAGIC data and GRACE(-FO) observations
nodes.venue: GRACE/GRACE-FO Science Team Meeting 2026
nodes.abstract: Terrestrial Water Storage Anomalies (TWSA) derived from satellite gravimetry provide a unique, spatially integrated measure of large-scale hydrological conditions and are widely used to characterize basin-scale wet and dry states. However, their applicability to regional hydrological monitoring remains limited by their coarse spatial resolution, which hampers the detection of localized storage anomalies relevant to flood onset, evolution, and groundwater variability.Here, it is investigated an unsupervised deep-learning framework based on convolutional neural networks to enhance the spatial resolution of TWSA products across simulated and real mission scenarios. The method relies on a U-Net architecture driven by ERA5-Land hydro-climatic variables, and is first applied to end-to-end closed-loop simulations of the NGGM and MAGIC next-generation gravity missions. Particular attention is given to 5-daily solutions, which represent a key expected advancement of future gravimetric constellations compared with the monthly solutions currently provided by GRACE(-FO). In this setting, simulated TWSA fields are downscaled from 3° to 1°, while monthly 2° simulations are also considered to assess the framework under GRACE-like temporal conditions. For the syntetic products, the downscaled fields are validated using the ESA Earth System Model 3.0 as the reference signal.Results show that the downscaled products preserve consistency with native gravimetric observations while recovering finer-scale spatial structures. To assess transferability, the same pipeline is applied to real GRACE(-FO) observations, downscaling monthly 3° TWSA products into 1° maps.The framework is also extended to GRACE-derived groundwater storage anomalies (GWSA) over France, downscaled from 0.5° to 0.1° and evaluated against independent in situ groundwater observations.Finally, downscaled synthetic TWSA fields are exploited for extreme-event monitoring using threshold-based indicators derived from climatological anomalies. The analysis assesses whether the increased spatial resolution retains localized anomaly patterns otherwise smoothed at coarse scales, supporting the monitoring of flood-prone conditions.

nodes.abstract: Abstract We present a multiwavelength analysis of the radio transient VT J1906+0849, discovered as a 70 mJy source in Epoch 1 of the Very Large Array Sky Survey (VLASS), 21 yr after an NRAO VLA Sky Survey (NVSS) nondetection. Radio observations reveal the source was first detected in 2005, peaking at ≳200 mJy in 2014, then declining until a late 2025 rebrightening. The transient sits at a Galactic latitude of ≈0.74 ∘ and the properties of its optical-infrared counterpart support a Galactic origin. At d ≳ 15 kpc, the extreme radio luminosity is likely powered by sustained accretion onto a compact object. However, a Swift-XRT nondetection shows it is X-ray faint relative to the Galactic X-ray binary population, and the radio emission is distinct from X-ray binaries in its temporal and spectral behavior. Broadband radio spectra suggest synchrotron self-absorption, but size constraints from equipartition and very long baseline interferometry show little to no expansion in the radio-emitting region over 5 yr, despite significant spectral evolution. Near-infrared spectroscopy reveals a single broad emission line with a stable centroid but variable width and luminosity. We attribute this feature to blueshifted Br γ tracing a persistent asymmetric ≈2000 km s −1 outflow. These properties are unlike any previously identified Galactic radio source. One possible interpretation is that VT J1906+0849 is a young analog of the microquasar SS 433, with a dense disk wind confining a continuously powered synchrotron outflow. This jet–wind interaction explains the compact, slowly expanding radio source and may contribute to the absence of bright X-ray emission.
